//! A second `base_s` declared in an `extern` block. It has no body, so it
//! can hold no read, and a rule that recognises declarations by their
//! source line will not see it at all — this is the false GREEN of the
//! superseded column rule.

fn base_s() -> i64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("clock")
        .as_secs() as i64
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn base_s() -> i64;
}
